newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB -5-mo 97 premium income up 5.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: AMB -5-mo 97 premium income up 5.4 pct.

text.p: German insurer Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs-AG (AMB) said on Wednesday that its total premium income in the first five months of 1997 rose 5.4 percent to 7.8 billion marks.

The group said premium income in damage and accident insurance fell by 0.1 percent in the period, while life insurance new business grew above average by 3.5 percent. Health insurance also increased in the period.
AMB, one of Germany's leading insurance groups, said it expected satisfactory growth levels in full-year 1997.

The group said it expected to at least match last year's group profits provided there was not a drastic increase in claims and capital markets remained stable. In 1996 AMB reported a group net profit of 343.3 million marks.
The insurer also said it expected to pay an unchanged dividend in full-year 1997 despite an increase in base capital. In 1996 the dividend payout was increased to 16 marks per share from 15 marks.
AMB is planning to raise new capital as part of a restructuring.
